transcript.text: the door on our built in dishwasher just crashes down when you open it now, used to stay put. Hotpoint I think

That sounds like the door balance springs or hinge cables have worn out, which is the most common cause of a door crashing down instead of staying put. It could also be a loose hinge or something physically blocking it from closing fully. To help us narrow this down, please switch off and unplug the dishwasher first for safety. Then open the door and check if the springs at the top corners look intact or detached, and see if anything in the racks is sticking out to stop it closing. Let me know what you find with those two checks.

Done, it's unplugged. The door closes and latches fine and nothing's sticking out. With a torch under the plinth I can see a loose spring hanging down on the right side. Left side still has some tension, right has none.

That loose spring on the right side is almost certainly why your door crashes down, as the balance is no longer holding it up. Since you've identified this, we need to find the correct replacement part for your specific Hotpoint model. Could you please provide the model number so I can help you locate the right spring? It's usually found on a label on the side edge of the door or inside the door frame. If you can't reach it because the door won't open properly, don't worry about it just yet.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
The sticker on the door edge is partly peeled, so all I can read is that it starts with LTF. It's a Hotpoint, 6 years old. Is that enough to go on?

Yes, that's enough for us to move forward with confidence. The loose spring you found on the right side is the most likely cause of your door crashing down.
